patient.name: Marcus Deline
patient.chiefComplaint: Decreased level of consciousness after assault

history.hpi: Bystanders report the patient was struck multiple times in the head and face during an altercation outside a bar, with a brief loss of consciousness. He regained some responsiveness, vomited twice, and has become progressively less responsive and unable to protect his airway since police arrived.
history.lastOralIntake: Alcohol and bar food approximately 2 hours prior to the assault
history.events: Struck multiple times during a physical altercation outside a bar; bystanders called 911 and police secured the scene before EMS arrival

scene.dispatch: 28-year-old male, assault victim, decreased level of consciousness, outside a bar
scene.location: Sidewalk outside a bar, patient supine near the entrance
scene.safety: Scene secured by police; assailant left prior to EMS arrival
scene.bystanders: Bar patrons and a bouncer report he was struck several times in the head and face, briefly lost consciousness, then vomited twice before becoming less responsive
visualCues: Laceration and rising hematoma over the right temporal/parietal scalp
Blood-tinged emesis pooled near the mouth
Empty beer bottles and a overturned bar stool nearby
Patient not following commands, moaning to painful stimuli

phases.name: Initial Contact
phases.description: Crew arrives to find a 28-year-old male supine outside a bar with visible head trauma, decreased level of consciousness, and blood-tinged emesis in the oropharynx. He is moaning and withdrawing to pain but not following commands or protecting his airway.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Vomiting, poor secretion control, gurgling respirations, blood-tinged emesis in oropharynx
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil 5mm sluggish, right pupil 3mm reactive
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws and localizes to painful stimuli; no purposeful movement to command
otherFindings: Rising hematoma and laceration over right temporal/parietal scalp
Blood-tinged emesis in oropharynx, active gurgling
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Moans to painful stimuli; no verbal output

transitions.condition: Crew performs a primary survey, recognizes GCS 7 with inadequate airway protection and active vomiting meeting RSI criteria, and begins high-flow oxygenation and C-spine stabilization in preparation for drug-assisted airway management.

phases.name: Preoxygenated for RSI
phases.description: Crew suctions the airway, applies high-flow oxygen via non-rebreather, maintains cervical spine stabilization, and preoxygenates with positive pressure ventilation for at least two minutes while confirming blood pressure is adequate before proceeding to drug-assisted intubation.
phases.triggerCondition: After the primary survey and C-spine stabilization, the crew recognizes GCS 7 with inadequate airway protection and active vomiting, meeting criteria for RSI. The patient is preoxygenated for at least two minutes and blood pressure is checked prior to any sedative or paralytic administration.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Suctioned clear of blood and emesis, NRB in place
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil 5mm sluggish, right pupil 3mm reactive
clinicalPresentation.motorFunction: Withdraws and localizes to painful stimuli
otherFindings: Cervical collar applied, manual stabilization maintained
Two minutes of high-flow preoxygenation completed
Repeat BP confirms SBP above 110 mmHg threshold
clinicalPresentation.patientSpeech: Moans to painful stimuli; no verbal output

expectedActions.shortAction: Apply high-flow O2 via NRB; suction blood/emesis from oropharynx
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer high-flow oxygen via NRB (non-rebreather) as a precaution against unanticipated deterioration.
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents hypoxia and aspiration prior to advanced airway management.

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain cervical spine stabilization; assume concomitant C-spine injury
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assume concomitant cervical spine injury in patients with moderate/severe head injury
expectedActions.rationale: Blunt head trauma with altered mentation carries high risk of concurrent cervical injury.

expectedActions.shortAction: Preoxygenate with high-flow O2 + PPV for at least 2 minutes before RSI attempt
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Patient should be pre-oxygenated with high flow oxygen, and positive pressure ventilation for a minimum of two minutes prior to the procedure.
expectedActions.rationale: Extends the safe apnea window during the intubation attempt and prevents peri-intubation hypoxia.

expectedActions.shortAction: Reassess BP before sedative/paralytic; treat to maintain SBP ≥110 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Assess the patient's blood pressure prior to the administration of any medication that may cause hypotension. Adult (age greater than 10 years): maintain SBP greater than or equal to 110 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Hypotension worsens cerebral perfusion and secondary brain injury in TBI.

transitions.condition: After confirming two minutes of preoxygenation and an adequate blood pressure, the crew proceeds with premedication, induction, and paralysis for RSI.
Crew proceeds directly to sedative/paralytic administration without completing the required two-minute high-flow preoxygenation period.

phases.name: RSI performed, tube confirmed
phases.description: Crew administers fentanyl premedication, etomidate for induction, and rocuronium for paralysis, then successfully intubates and confirms tube placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds.
phases.triggerCondition: After adequate preoxygenation and blood pressure optimization, the crew proceeds with drug-assisted intubation: fentanyl premedication, etomidate induction, rocuronium paralysis, followed by laryngoscopy and endotracheal intubation confirmed by waveform capnography.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Endotracheal tube in place, confirmed by waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil 5mm sluggish, right pupil 3mm reactive

expectedActions.shortAction: Fentanyl 85 mcg IV premedication (85 kg × 1 mcg/kg), 2–3 min prior to intubation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Consider pre-medication with Fentanyl, 1 mcg/kg, 2-3 minutes prior to intubation attempt.
expectedActions.rationale: Blunts the sympathetic/ICP response to laryngoscopy.

expectedActions.shortAction: Etomidate 25 mg IV push induction (85 kg × 0.3 mg/kg = 25.5 mg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer induction sedative agent: Etomidate IV push, 0.2-0.3 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Hemodynamically neutral induction agent appropriate for a TBI patient.

expectedActions.shortAction: Rocuronium 85 mg IV push paralytic (85 kg × 1 mg/kg)
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Administer paralytic agent: Succinylcholine IV push, 1-2 mg/kg OR Rocuronium IV push, 1 mg/kg OR Vecuronium IV push, 0.1 mg/kg
expectedActions.rationale: Provides paralysis for first-pass intubation success.

expectedActions.shortAction: Intubate; confirm placement with waveform capnography and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Confirm placement of advanced airway (endotracheal tube, SGA) with waveform capnography (most reliable), absent gastric sounds, and bilateral breath sounds
expectedActions.rationale: Waveform capnography is the most reliable confirmation of correct tube placement.

expectedActions.shortAction: Ventilate at 10 breaths/min; target EtCO2 35–45 mmHg, avoid hyperventilation
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Do not induce hypocapnia through hyper-/overventilation. Maintain all patients in EtCO2 range of 35–45 mmHg
expectedActions.rationale: Hyperventilation causes cerebral vasoconstriction and worsens secondary brain injury.

transitions.condition: Ventilation rate is maintained at 10 breaths/min with EtCO2 held in the 35-45 mmHg range; patient is packaged for transport.
Crew ventilates faster than the protocol-directed rate, driving EtCO2 below 30 mmHg and risking cerebral vasoconstriction.

phases.name: Ventilation controlled, transport
phases.description: Tube is secured, sedation is maintained, ventilation rate is controlled to keep EtCO2 in the target range, and the patient is transported to a trauma center capable of managing severe TBI.
phases.triggerCondition: Tube secured, sedation maintained, and ventilation rate controlled to EtCO2 35-45 mmHg; patient transported to the highest level of trauma care available.

clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil 5mm sluggish, right pupil 3mm reactive, trended and documented

expectedActions.shortAction: Maintain post-intubation sedation; reassess RASS/comfort en route
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Intubated patients should be provided appropriate sedation with sedative or opioid medications, and sedation titrated to an appropriate target level using RASS score or similar scale
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents patient agitation, tube displacement, and rises in ICP.

expectedActions.shortAction: Transport to highest level trauma center per GCS 3–13 criteria
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Preferential transport to highest level of care within trauma system: GCS 3–13, P (pain) or U (unresponsive) on AVPU scale
expectedActions.rationale: Severe TBI requires definitive neurosurgical capability.

phases.name: RSI attempted without adequate preoxygenation
phases.description: Crew skips the required two-minute preoxygenation period and proceeds directly to sedation and paralysis. SpO2 falls rapidly during the intubation attempt.
phases.triggerCondition: Crew proceeds directly to sedative/paralytic administration without the required two-minute high-flow preoxygenation period; SpO2 falls rapidly during the intubation attempt.

clinicalPresentation.airway: Laryngoscope in place, tube not yet passed
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil 5mm sluggish, right pupil 3mm reactive
otherFindings: SpO2 falling rapidly during the attempt

expectedActions.shortAction: Abort attempt at SpO2 <90%; resume BVM with PEEP to reoxygenate
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Attempt intubation, limiting attempts to 15 seconds, or a desaturation below 90%, whichever occurs first.
expectedActions.rationale: Prevents hypoxic secondary brain injury and hypoxic cardiac arrest.

phases.name: Hyperventilation drives EtCO2 low
phases.description: Ventilation rate exceeds the protocol-directed target after intubation, driving EtCO2 below 30 mmHg and risking cerebral vasoconstriction that worsens secondary brain injury.
phases.triggerCondition: Ventilation rate exceeds protocol targets after intubation; EtCO2 drifts below 30 mmHg, risking cerebral vasoconstriction and worsened secondary brain injury.

clinicalPresentation.breathing: Ventilated at an excessive rate, approximately 20/min
clinicalPresentation.pupils: Left pupil now 6mm and minimally reactive, right pupil 3mm reactive
otherFindings: Left pupil dilation progressing — early herniation concern

expectedActions.shortAction: Reduce ventilation rate to 10/min; retarget EtCO2 to 35–45 mmHg
expectedActions.protocolExcerpt: Do not induce hypocapnia through hyper-/overventilation. Hyperventilation results in vasoconstriction which further decreases blood flow to the brain and worsens the secondary brain injury.
expectedActions.rationale: Correcting the ventilation rate reverses iatrogenic cerebral vasoconstriction.
